why: BOTH N/A branches of this rule in a single case, one per folder — the folders are called `pass` and `fail` by inheritance from the format, and here each isolates a different branch. `pass/` has the lint and test scripts and no workflow: the one that charges for the existence of CI is the `ci` rule, and charging twice for the same absence measures the same thing twice and fails the repository double. `fail/` has a workflow and a package.json whose only script is `empacotar`: the rule only charges for what the repository HAS, because demanding `lint` from someone who has no lint is demanding the adoption of a tool, a decision of another level. Either of the two turning into `passou` makes the case accuse.
